items.title: Why We’ve Been Looking at the Hotel Brands vs. OTAs War All Wrong
items.summary: The hotel industry’s distribution war has an overlooked third party: the owner. New questions about AI, loyalty and customer acquisition could make that imbalance even more consequential.

items.title: How Travel Credit Cards Are Becoming Full-Trip Companions: Watch Video
items.summary: Travel credit cards are moving well beyond points and booking. At Skift Global Forum, Capital One Travel’s Sarah Moore said the opportunity lies in remaining useful throughout the trip by combining context, experiences, technology, and trust to build deeper relationships with tra

items.title: Delta CEO Ed Bastian Slams ‘Short-Sighted’ Heathrow Shake-Up
items.summary: Virgin Atlantic's anger over Heathrow's terminal shake-up now has heavyweight backing from Atlanta. With Ed Bastian joining the fight, the airport faces mounting pressure to rethink its plans.

items.title: Gulf Hotels’ Peak Season Stalls as Travelers Wait Out the U.S. Midterms
items.summary: Bookings for the Gulf’s peak quarter are on hold until after the U.S. vote. With airlines still staying away, some operators don’t expect a real recovery until late 2027.

items.title: Skift Aviation Forum 2026: Five Decisions in the Room
items.summary: Jet fuel prices are still rising, and just about every variable affecting air travel is in flux — aircraft supply, air traffic volume, global partnerships, input costs. Decisions made today will determine who succeeds in aviation.

items.title: Skift Commerce Summit 2026: Five Decisions in the Room
items.summary: AI agents are here. Travel isn't ready. Decisions made today will determine who controls the booking, the customer relationship, and the economics of travel commerce.

items.title: Choice Hotels Narrows Its Revenue Gap, but Its Upscale Brands Still Trail
items.summary: CEO Dom Dragisich can claim a win in budget hotels, with Choice recently outperforming the industry average. But upscale brands grew at a much lower pace than the industry averages.

items.title: Marriott’s Fees Jump 14% as Hotel Owners Seek a Bigger Cut
items.summary: Marriott said that its talks with hotel owners who want a bigger cut of the pie have been "constructive." It's easier for everyone to stay polite about the fee math when profit growth has revived significantly.
